questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, what should you do?

options.text: Look toward the center of the road.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This prevents you from being blinded by the bright headlights and lets you see enough of the road to stay safe. Do not flash your own bright lights in response.

questions.question: Another car is following you too closely on a two-lane road. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down gradually to let the tailgater pass.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake suddenly, then resume your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually to let the tailgater pass.
questions.explanation: Slow down gradually. This encourages the tailgater to pass you. If you can, move to another lane first. Never brake suddenly, as this is dangerous.

questions.question: You are being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Use the right lane unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than traffic, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: When a bicyclist turns left, what can they do?

options.text: Use the left lane.
Cut through all lanes.
Wait on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists drive with traffic on the road. It is normal to see a bicyclist in the left lane when turning left.

questions.question: The best way to avoid a dangerous situation is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes ahead of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Be aware of everything around your vehicle at all times. Watch the front, sides, and rear. This helps you spot problems early and react safely.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the road or pavement edge. What should you do?

options.text: When safe, gradually steer back onto the road.
Turn back onto the road immediately.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: When safe, gradually steer back onto the road.
questions.explanation: Do not turn sharply back onto the road right away. Slow down, check traffic, and gradually steer back when it is safe.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a walk signal.

questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all vehicles moving through the intersection.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, you check for a gap, match traffic speed, and signal. What is next?

options.text: Expect other drivers to let you in since you signaled.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to completely clear.

questions.explanation: Merge carefully when it is safe. Watch other traffic closely. Do not expect drivers to clear the lane for you.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed.
Lanes move in the same direction and passing is allowed.
Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: A solid white line means you cannot cross it to pass or change lanes. White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction.

questions.question: To avoid sudden braking or turning, look ahead ____ seconds.

options.text: 3 seconds
10 seconds
15 seconds

questions.explanation: Look at least 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to see hazards and make safe choices. Other drivers will have more time to react to your moves.

questions.question: Your car is skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Do not turn the steering wheel.
Turn the steering wheel left.
Turn the steering wheel right.

questions.explanation: Turn the wheel in the direction of the skid. Release the gas and do not brake. If you have anti-lock brakes, press the brake hard and steer straight.

questions.question: How do you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep your eyes on the center line.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights. Then look ahead again to watch the other vehicle's position.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: Create extra space ahead when being tailgated. Slow down gradually or change lanes. Never brake suddenly, as this can cause a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic from the right.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions ahead. This sign tells you that traffic will merge from the right side. Be ready to let them in safely.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with its siren and lights on while you are crossing an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or sirens, finish crossing. Then drive to the right and stop. You must yield to all police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or lights.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should you turn into?

options.text: Turn into any lane.
Turn into first lane.
Turn into second lane.

questions.explanation: When turning, go from your lane into the first available legal lane ahead. When turning from a two-way to a one-way street, turn into the first lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
The road ahead winds with a series of turns or curves.
Slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when wet and is harder to drive on safely.

questions.question: When is it legal to turn left at a red light after stopping?

options.text: You are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.
You are traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you may turn left at a red light only when going from a one-way street to another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs that forbid this turn.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid out of control, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Stay off the brakes.

questions.explanation: If your car skids, do not use the brakes. Steer to get control back. Keep steering until your car is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Prepare to stop, if needed.
Maintain a steady speed.

questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. A car may be stalled just out of sight. You must be able to stop. Slow down when approaching hills or curves so you can stop if necessary.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly on snow or ice. The ABS will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, how can you reduce the chance of an accident?

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic (within posted speed limits). Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes often happen when drivers go different speeds.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not permitted.
Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline allows you to cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if no cars are coming. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: In bad weather, what should you do?

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid hard braking and sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when rain first starts. When the road is slippery, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid making turns and stops while driving at high speeds.
Test your tires' traction while going uphill.
Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making turns and stops while driving at high speeds.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. Drive slower on wet roads than on dry roads. Avoid fast turns or stops to prevent skidding.
